newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rises on overseas rebound and Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rises on overseas rebound and Nokia.

text.p: Shares rose on Wednesday as trade livened up in the afternoon, partly boosted by interest related to an options expiry on Thursday, brokers said.
The HEX advanced 1.37 percent to 2,414.91 in volume at 417 million markka, quite lively for the pre-Christmas period.
Sentiment was encouraged by Wall Street's advances overnight and early on Wednesday. "We're up nicely, and New York also opened higher," one broker said.
Nokia tracked Ericsson higher amid rumours about a planned merger of the two rivals, which some brokers dismissed.
"I don't believe that of course, but it has moved the shares," said one. Nokia ended up 7.00 markka at 255.00 and Ericsson in late trade added 9.50 crowns to 206.0.
"There's been talk of Ericsson and Nokia merging, but that should be taken with a pinch of salt," one broker said, adding that the rumours came from London.
Brokers mentioned big volume in forest industry group UPM-Kymmene as a result of trade ahead of options expiry.
"I think the high volume in UPM is due to stocks futures and options expiring tomorrow," one said. UPM closed flat at 94.00 markka and volume was 36 million markka.
Metsa-Serla pared Tuesday's losses, addding 1.00 markka or over three percent to 33.00 markka, as confidence in its recent acquisitions improved.
